chapters.summary: At Valmiki's hermitage the first verse is born from grief. Stepping into the story, you walk with Vishvamitra, Rama and Lakshmana, free Tataka's forest and guard the sacrifice at Siddhashrama.

signs.text: Valmiki's hut. Guests are always welcome.
East: the road beyond the hermitage. Those who walk it with a verse in their heart step into the story.
South: the ford of the Tamasa.
The ford of the Tamasa. Bathe in peace.
West: back to the hermitage of Valmiki, outside the story.
East: the forest of Tataka. Travellers, turn back!

cmds.say: Listen well, child. A great story is about to be born.
Go on ahead, {player}. The ford is just south of the hermitage. I will follow you.

cmds.objective: Go south to the bank of the Tamasa.

then.say: Learn the new verse by heart with Bharadvaja, child. Speak with him.

else.say: Bharadvaja wishes to test you, child. Speak with him.
Look how clear the water is today.

cmds.say: A pair of krauncha birds, singing to each other.
A hunter crouches in the bushes, bow in hand.
The Tamasa keeps her own counsel. But since that morning, she seems to murmur in verse.
At the ford the Tamasa runs clear over white sand. Valmiki and Bharadvaja are already waiting.
Look, Bharadvaja. This water is as clear as the mind of a good person. Set down the water pot; I will bathe here.
In a tree by the water, a pair of krauncha birds sing to each other, never apart.
Then a {w:nishada} (hunter) looses an arrow from the bushes. The male bird falls to the sand, and his mate cries out over him.
Valmiki's heart fills with pity. Words rise out of his grief, measured and whole.
What have I spoken? It came from grief, and it has become a verse.
Four quarters, eight syllables in each, fit to be sung to the strings of the vina. Let it be called a verse, and nothing else.

then.say: Say the first quarter with me, {player}.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Every word has its meaning on the verse card. Look again when you can.

cmds.say: Keep these two words close: the first two words of the verse. Tap any word on a card to see what it means.
A cold wind sweeps over the river. Smoke-dark shapes rise from the reeds, and the words of the new verse scatter like startled birds.
Teacher, the words! They are flying away!
This is illusion: a shadow that hates the story before it is even told. It has scattered every verse I am yet to sing.
{player}, take this palm-leaf book. Every verse you hear will be written in it, and every word you learn will gather there.
You received the palm-leaf book of verses!

then.say: Bharadvaja, learn this new verse by heart, and teach it to our young friend too. Then we walk back.

else.say: Bharadvaja, test our young friend. A verse is only truly ours when we can defend it.

then.objective: Talk to Bharadvaja and learn the new verse by heart.

else.objective: Talk to Bharadvaja for a friendly verse-debate.

then.say: A debate of verses! Every move you make is a question about the words you have heard. Answer well, and your argument lands.
Answer swiftly and perfectly, and it lands even harder. Ready?
The teacher's new verse! Let us learn it by heart first, then walk back.
I say a line, and you say it after me. Where a word is missing, tap the right one.

battle.intro: Bharadvaja challenges you to a friendly verse-debate!

then.say: Now the verse lives in two memories. Let us tell the guru.

else.say: I am persuaded! You really did hear every word.

then.say: You nearly had me! Every wrong answer shows you the right word, so you learn either way.
You nearly had me! When you forget a word, the line shows you the right one, so you learn either way.
I heard you both, and I am pleased. Come back to the hermitage now, {player}. At the shrine you will recite the verse and make it whole again.

else.say: Well argued, both of you. Come back to the hermitage now, {player}. At the shrine you will recite the verse and make it whole again.

then.objective: Return to the hermitage and talk to Valmiki at the shrine.

else.say: The teacher wants to bathe here. Is the water not clear today?

then.say: Listen! The verse lives again. Born of grief, it is now a mantra you can speak in battle.
Your verse is restored. You can now use the move {n:move.shoka_shloka}. Check your moves in the party menu.
The poem I will compose tells of Rama, the man Narada described. The illusion has scattered its words through the whole tale.
Go into the story, {player}. Walk beside Rama, hear each verse where it is spoken, and restore it at a shrine. The east gate will open for you.

then.objective: Go through the east gate into the story.

else.say: The verse is whole again. Go east through the gate and step into the story. Rama is waiting on the road.

else.objective: Go through the east gate into the story.

else.say: This is the hermitage shrine. Here you may rest, save your journey, and recite the verses you have heard.

then.say: There is a study hall here too, for practising words. Go there only when you wish.

else.say: To recite is to put the scattered words back in their places, quarter by quarter. Recite the verse of the krauncha for me.

then.say: Listen! The verse lives again. Born of grief, it is now a mantra you can speak in battle.
Your verse is restored. You can now use the move {n:move.shoka_shloka}. Check your moves in the party menu.
The poem I will compose tells of Rama, the man Narada described. The illusion has scattered its words through the whole tale.
Go into the story, {player}. Walk beside Rama, hear each verse where it is spoken, and restore it at a shrine. The east gate will open for you.

then.objective: Go through the east gate into the story.

else.say: Some words are still out of place. Do not worry: rest, look at the verse card again, and recite it for me once more.
Take your time, child. Speak to me again when you are ready.

then.say: The path east shimmers like heat over sand. Valmiki calls after you: "Restore the verse at the shrine first, child. Talk to me there when you are ready."

then.objective: Talk to Valmiki at the shrine and recite the verse.

then.say: The path east shimmers like heat over sand. Not yet: Bharadvaja is waiting for you on the riverbank to the south.

then.objective: Talk to Bharadvaja and learn the new verse by heart.

else.objective: Talk to Bharadvaja for a friendly verse-debate.

else.say: The path east shimmers like heat over sand. Something tells you it is not time yet. Valmiki is going down to the river, south of the hermitage.

else.objective: Go south to the bank of the Tamasa.

then.say: Did you know? Each word you answer correctly grows stronger in your word book. Words you miss come back more often, until they stick.
Did you know? Each line you recite in battle stays with you. A line you forget comes back more often, until it sticks.
Here, take these for the road. Fruit restores a tired hero.
You received 3 fruits.

cmds.say: Fruit from the village orchards and honey from the forest. Honey refreshes the mind, so your heroes can call on their mantras again.
Fresh water from the well! The sage says a clear mind is like clear water: you can see all the way to the bottom.
Psst! Sanskrit can be shown in Devanagari, or in Roman letters with little marks. Pick the script in your Samskuru profile settings. I like Devanagari!
The cows were restless last night, as if a shadow walked among the trees. Stay on the path, young one.
I came with Narada and stayed to listen. What a night of words!

then.say: Take some honey with you. A reciter needs a sweet voice.
You received 1 honey.

cmds.say: I am sweeping the teacher's hut. He says even sweeping can be done with a whole heart.
Your word book, {n:ui.words}, keeps every word you have met. It shows how well you know each one: unseen, seen, known, and mastered.
Tap a Sanskrit word in someone's speech to see what it means.

then.say: Did you hear the teacher's verse at the river? Let me say what it means, to check I have it right.
'Hunter, may you find no lasting place for endless years, because you killed one of the krauncha pair, lost in love.'
The first word, {w:ma}, means "may you not". And {w:nishada} is the hunter. The whole verse is a wish, born of grief!

cmds.say: When I recite, I go quarter by quarter. Eight syllables, then the next eight. It is like climbing steps!
You step through the gate, and the world turns like a page.
You stand on the bank of the Sarayu in the {w:sandhya} (twilight) before dawn. Two young men sleep on beds of leaves, and a sage in white sits beside them.
Who are you, child? You have the look of a student from a poet's hermitage.

then.choice: Vishvamitra asks: "Who are you, child? Where do you come from?"

options.label: I am going east, to the forest.

then.say: East, with us? Good. But I asked who you are, and where you come from.
Let them sleep a little longer. But tell me about yourself, child.

cmds.say: You tell the sage of Valmiki, of the verse, and of the scattered words.
I am Vishvamitra. King Dasharatha has entrusted his sons to me, to guard my sacrifice from the night-wanderers. Watch, and listen.
The sage rises and gently wakes the elder prince.
We are awake, revered teacher. First the morning prayers, and then the road.
And who is this? A friend from the forest?
A student of the poet who will one day sing of you. Let the child walk with us.
Rama joins your party!
Lakshmana joins your party!

onCorrect.say: Well said. My teacher will be pleased with you.

onWrong.say: Close! Look at the verse card again. Each word is explained there.

then.say: Sacred kusha grass grows tall along this road. Night-wanderers hide in it and may leap out as you walk through.
In battle, choose a move and answer its question. A correct answer makes the move land. A swift and perfect answer lands it harder.
Sacred kusha grass grows tall along this road. On this journey the night-wanderers in it stay hidden; only the battles of the story await you.
In battle, choose a move. For an astra, recite a line of its verse. Other moves are simple.
If a word is missing from the line, choose it with one tap. A line you know well recites itself.

cmds.objective: Follow the road east toward the forest.

cmds.say: Come, the day has begun.
The prince sleeps peacefully on a bed of leaves.

then.say: May the road be kind to you. Rest at Vishvamitra's hermitage when you reach it.

else.say: So this is the prince the sage Narada sang of! I heard him once, by the Ganga.
Narada said Rama is like the {w:samudra} (ocean) in depth and like the {w:himavat} (Himalaya) in steadiness. Listen.

onCorrect.say: Just so! Words like these are the arrows of a reciter.

onWrong.say: Look again at the card in your verse book. Each word has its meaning beside it.

else.say: The sage gives you 2 fruits.

then.say: If you get hurt in the tall grass, eat some fruit from your bag. And the hermitage shrines will always restore you.
If you get hurt in a battle, eat some fruit from your bag. And the hermitage shrines will always restore you.

cmds.say: In a fight, a tired hero can switch places with a fresh one. Every hero who takes part learns from the battle.

then.say: Go, Rama. Free this land of its fear.

else.say: Stop here, princes. Beyond these trees lies a forest that was once two rich countries. No one lives there now.
It is haunted by Tataka, a yakshi with the strength of a thousand elephants. The sage Agastya cursed her, and her son Maricha with her.
Teacher, she is a woman. Must I raise my bow against her?
A king's son protects those who cannot protect themselves, Rama. That is his {w:dharma} (duty). She has emptied this whole land of people.
My father told me to obey your word. For the sake of the people and the sages, I will do as you say.
Then rest a moment first. That forest is dark even at noon.

else.objective: Enter Tataka's forest to the east and face Tataka.

cmds.say: Vishvamitra calls after you: "Wait, princes! Hear what lies ahead before you go in."
A roar shakes the trees. Dust and stones rain down from the darkness ahead.
Brother, she is coming!

cmds.objective: Face Tataka at the far side of the clearing.

cmds.say: You go to face Tataka? Then take this {w:oshadhi} (healing herb). It can rouse a hero who is exhausted.

then.say: You received 1 healing herb.

else.say: May the gods guard you.

cmds.say: Tataka's forest is ours! Turn back, or fight!

battle.intro: A night-wanderer leaps out of the dark!

onWin.say: The night-wanderer melts back into the shadows.

cmds.say: A shape as vast as a storm cloud bursts out of the darkness, hurling rocks and dust.
Now, Rama! For the sake of the people!

then.say: By her illusion she will rain stones on you. When she makes ready, guard yourselves, or recite a verse!

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

battle.intro: Tataka rises out of the darkness!

onWin.say: Rama's arrow strikes true, and Tataka falls like a mountain.
Silence. Then birdsong, for the first time in years. The forest is free.
Well done, my son. I am pleased with you.
Take the divine weapons that I hold: the {n:move.agneyastra}, the {n:move.varunastra}, the {n:move.vayavyastra}, and many more.
Vishvamitra teaches Rama the mantras of the divine weapons. They will answer Rama as he grows in strength.

then.say: The same astra, loosed again and again, grows tired. Choose another astra!

onWin.objective: Go east to Vishvamitra's hermitage, Siddhashrama.

cmds.say: The land breathes again. Come, my hermitage lies just to the east.
Siddhashrama: the hermitage where Vishnu once performed his austerities, before he was born as the dwarf Vamana. Vishvamitra's disciples run to greet him.
Princes, today I begin my sacrifice. For six days and nights I will keep a vow of silence.
Guard the altar well. On the last night, the night-wanderers will come.
Vishvamitra takes his seat before the fire and speaks no more.

cmds.objective: Prepare at the shrine, then speak to the disciple at the altar.

then.say: The sacrifice is complete, thanks to you all.

else.say: Vishvamitra sits before the sacred fire, eyes closed, keeping his vow of silence.

then.say: The fire burns peacefully now. Thank you, friends.
Five days have passed in peace. Tonight is the sixth night, the last. Are the princes ready?

then.choice: Stand guard on the last night?

options.label: Rest and save, then stand guard

then.say: The sacred fire leaps up. Then the sky darkens, and with a roar the night-wanderers come, led by Subahu and Maricha.
Lakshmana, stand with me. They shall not touch the altar.
See, Lakshmana: the weapon of Manu will throw Maricha far into the ocean, and Agni's weapon will strike down Subahu.
If they make ready to rain blood on the altar, raise your guard, brother!

battle.intro: Subahu and Maricha descend upon the sacrifice!

onWin.say: Rama looses the weapon of Manu at Maricha. It does not kill him: it carries him a hundred leagues away and drops him, stunned, into the ocean.
With the fire weapon Rama strikes down Subahu, and the other night-wanderers flee into the dark.
At dawn the sacrifice is complete, and Vishvamitra breaks his silence.
My purpose is fulfilled, Rama. You have honoured your father's word. Truly this is now the hermitage of fulfilment.
From Siddhashrama, Vishvamitra led the princes to Mithila. There Rama lifted the great bow of Shiva and broke it, and King Janaka gave him his daughter Sita in marriage.
Many happy years passed in Ayodhya. So ends the first book, the Book of Youth.
From far away, you hear Valmiki's voice: "Well done, {player}. Turn the page. The next book begins in Ayodhya."

onWin.objective: Walk into Ayodhya to begin Book 2.

else.say: Rest at the shrine and make ready. We will wait for you.
Welcome, friends.

cmds.say: Even hermits need supplies! Roots and herbs from the forest, gathered with care.
Long ago, Vishnu did his penance here before he was born as Vamana. This is a place where good efforts bear fruit.
Vishvamitra was once a king. He gave up his throne and won the rank of a great sage through long austerity.
If he trusts the princes to guard his sacrifice, they must be extraordinary.
I memorise verses by saying them in quarters. A recited verse that is perfect turns gold in your verse book, {n:ui.verses}!
Wild rice and roots from the forest. Simple food for the sacrifice days.

then.say: You received 1 bundle of roots. Roots restore more strength than fruit.

cmds.say: When you restore a verse, a hero learns its power! I want to learn every verse in the poem.
A small chest is tucked between the trees. Some traveller left it for the next one.
You found 2 honey.
At the end of the grass trail sits an old chest, half hidden by roots.
You found 1 healing herb.
